mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE decreases, indicating a weak link between unemployment and equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% may signal tighter monetary policy, leading to decreased borrowing and investment, and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, indicating monetary policy is not a significant driver of equity returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 30% of instances when RSAFS increases, indicating consumer demand does not translate to equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) coupled with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) may indicate stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL rises, indicating stagflation does not negatively impact equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 35% of instances when PAYEMS increases, indicating labor market strength does not translate to equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong manufacturing sector, which may lead to increased economic output and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of instances when INDPRO increases, indicating manufacturing strength does not translate to equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) coupled with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) may indicate economic uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases and UNRATE rises, indicating economic uncertainty does not negatively impact equity performance.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) may indicate a tightening labor market with potential inflationary pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 35% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE declines, indicating monetary tightening does not lead to positive equity performance.
